hero.headline: Who Decides the Cord?
hero.subheadline: One evidence-based routine for the umbilical stump - plus the exact words to protect it from harmful 'remedies' without family war
hero.body: The baby's umbilical stump is still attached and must be kept clean and dry while relatives insist on traditional substances (toothpaste, shea butter, herbs, hot compresses) and hospital discharge instructions said something different. She does not know which daily care routine is actually safe, which traditional practices are harmless versus dangerous, and which changes in the stump's appearance mean 'normal healing' versus 'infection needing a doctor tonight'. A clear daily cord-care routine and red-flag triage your whole household follows, so everyone follows one rule and you know exactly when to see a doctor.
hero.trust_line: Educational content - not medical, clinical, or mental-health advice. Never diagnoses or treats. Any suspected infection goes to professional care the same day.
hero.evidence_label: Educational content informed by sourced research and clinical guidance. It is not a substitute for medical, clinical, or mental-health assessment.

before_state.label: Sound familiar?
before_state.headline: It is not that you are failing. The cord care just has no system.
paragraphs: Right now applying whatever substance the most senior relative recommends, cleaning the stump with multiple antiseptics, and covering the stump with belly bands or coins - and the people who matter most (mother, maternal/paternal grandmother (omugwo), partner, and community elders) are all pulling in different directions.
On top of that, stump kept moist under coverings, substances applied on top of hospital instructions, and no agreed household rule for who decides cord questions.
It feels like anxious every diaper change, afraid to contradict elders, and guilt and fear about causing infection.
Believes a preventable infection could kill her baby and that she would be blamed.
The cost: moist covered stumps heal slower, harmful substances introduced, and infection signs missed or over-reacted to.
before_state.punch: This is not a personal failing. It is a system gap - and Who Decides the Cord? closes it.

who_for.label: Fit check
who_for.headline: Read both sides before you buy.
who_for.intro: This system is built for a specific situation. If that is not you, it will not help - and we would rather tell you now.
for_items: Mother or primary caregiver of a newborn (0-3 weeks), in Nigeria/Africa or the diaspora, responsible for daily umbilical stump care - often with conflicting advice from grandmothers, aunties and hospital staff about what to apply and what to avoid

The baby's umbilical stump is still attached and must be kept clean and dry while relatives insist on traditional substances (toothpaste, shea butter, herbs, hot compresses) and hospital discharge instructions said something different

Tried following the grandmother's advice (e.g. applying toothpaste or tying a belly band) while secretly worrying; or cleaned with everything the pharmacy suggested because no one gave one clear routine
who_for.not_for_label: This is NOT for you if
not_for_items: This system coordinates everyday cord hygiene and triage ONLY. It never diagnoses infection, never treats with antibiotics, never advises removing the stump, and never replaces newborn wellness visits. Any suspected infection routes to professional care.

If any red flag is present (Redness spreading outward from the stump base onto the belly skin; Pus (yellow/green/white thick fluid) or foul smell; Swelling or hardening of skin around the stump), this is not a home system - seek professional care first.
who_for.note: This system coordinates everyday cord hygiene and triage ONLY.

promise.label: What we promise - and what we don't
promise.headline: A system. Not a guarantee.
promise.we_do: A clear daily cord-care routine and red-flag triage your whole household follows, so everyone follows one rule and you know exactly when to see a doctor. One clear, evidence-based daily routine; confidence to protect the stump from harmful substances without family war; and the exact red flags that mean seek care immediately.
promise.we_do_not: We do not promise: cannot diagnose infection remotely, does not replace newborn wellness visits, and some separation-time variation remains normal. This is an educational system, not medical, clinical, or mental-health care.
